mainTopic: Worshipped water, רבי יוחנן's three rulings for גבלא (ממזרים, wine, lupines and בישולי גוים), and a גוי carrying grapes to the winepress.
overview: The amud opens with רבי יוחנן's rule that public water does not become forbidden when a נכרי bows to it. This implies that privately owned water does become forbidden. The גמרא asks why this matters, since water is attached to the ground anyway. It answers that a wave lifted the water up. It then tries to use this to settle רבי יוחנן's view on boulders that broke loose by themselves, but rejects the proof by saying a person splashed the water up. Next comes a story: רבי חייא בר אבא saw lax practices in גבלא, and רבי יוחנן ordered three strict announcements, about ממזרים, diluted wine, and lupines cooked by gentiles. The גמרא explains each one, including a discussion of two versions of רב's rule on בישולי גוים. Finally, רב כהנא forbids a גוי to carry grapes to the winepress, and רב יימר begins a challenge from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Public water does not become forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, rules that water belonging to the public is not forbidden even if a נכרי worships it. The גמרא reads from this that an individual's water would become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: water that belongs to the public does not become forbidden. That implies that water belonging to one person does become forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רבי יוחנן about worshipped water and reads a hidden implication out of it. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason public water stays permitted is that one person cannot make forbidden something that belongs to everyone. The words 'הא דיחיד נאסרין' are the גמרא's own inference: if ownership is the reason, then privately owned water would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This implies…', used to draw an inference from what was just said

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
Water belonging to the public is not rendered forbidden.
This implies that water of an individual is rendered forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought as support for the earlier discussion on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Public water is not forbidden by worship. By implication, privately owned water is forbidden.

steps.title: Why not say water is attached to the ground?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needs the 'public' reason. Water is attached to the ground, and attached things are never forbidden by worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he could get the same result from the fact that water is attached to the ground!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the implication from step 1, that private water becomes forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that worshipping something attached to the ground (מחובר) does not make it forbidden. Water in a river or sea counts as attached. So even private water should be permitted, and the 'public' reason seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him derive it instead from…', meaning there is a simpler reason available

phrases.english: But let him derive it instead
from the fact that the water is attached to the ground!
phrases.notes: Things attached to the ground don't become forbidden when someone worships them, whoever owns them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference that private water becomes forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference 'הא דיחיד נאסרין' and the need for the 'public' reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water is מחובר, so it should be permitted no matter who owns it. That makes ownership irrelevant.

steps.title: A wave lifted the water
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is about water that a wave lifted and detached from the ground. Because it is no longer attached, only the 'public' reason can keep it permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for a case where a wave detached the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by narrowing the case: the water was no longer attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a wave lifts the water up, it is detached, so the 'attached' rule no longer protects it. Now ownership matters: public water stays permitted and private water becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is only needed for…', which narrows the ruling to a specific case

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
for a case where a wave detached the water.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water is still attached, so ownership does not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water was detached by a wave, so ownership is what decides.

steps.title: Proving רבי יוחנן's view on loosened boulders
steps.stepSummary: Water detached by a wave is like mountain boulders that broke loose by themselves. Since רבי יוחנן treats private water of this kind as forbidden, the גמרא wants to conclude that he is the one who forbids such boulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the end, this water is like mountain boulders that broke loose on their own. Should we conclude that רבי יוחנן is the one who says such boulders are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the previous answer and tries to use it to settle a different, open dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (46a) רבי יוחנן and the sons of רבי חייא argue about worshipping boulders that came loose with no human involvement, and we don't know who holds which view. Water lifted by a wave also came loose with no human involvement. If רבי יוחנן says private water like this becomes forbidden, he must hold that such boulders are forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the end', meaning 'either way, the result is still…'
Mountain boulders that came loose on their own
'Shall we conclude?', an attempt to settle an open question

phrases.english: In the end,
the water is like mountain boulders that came loose,
so shall we conclude that it is Rabbi Yoḥanan
who says such boulders are forbidden?
phrases.notes: This is the open dispute from earlier (46a) between רבי יוחנן and the sons of רבי חייא.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, אַבְנֵי הַר שֶׁנִּדַּלְדְּלוּ נִינְהוּ, תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר אֲסוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the wave answer to settle the boulders dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן is the one who forbids loosened boulders.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling about water, as explained in step 3 (detached by a wave).

steps.title: No proof: a person splashed the water
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The case is one where a person struck the water with his hand and detached it, so it is not like boulders that came loose on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for a case where someone splashed the water up with his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by changing who detached the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person detached the water, it counts as an ordinary detached object, and everyone agrees worship makes it forbidden if privately owned. This is a different case from the boulders, so רבי יוחנן could still hold that loosened boulders are permitted. The boulders question stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: Public water is never forbidden by worship. Private water is forbidden once a person detaches it from the ground. This סוגיא does not prove רבי יוחנן's view on boulders that came loose by themselves.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
for a case where he struck the water with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof attempted in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof about the boulders. The ruling about water stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the water came loose without a person. In fact a person detached it, which is unlike the boulders.

steps.title: What רבי חייא בר אבא saw in גבלא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא visits גבלא and sees three problems: Jewish women pregnant from half-converted gentiles, Jews drinking wine that gentiles diluted, and Jews eating lupines cooked by gentiles. He says nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא came to גבלא. He saw Jewish women pregnant from gentiles who had been circumcised but had not immersed. He saw wine that gentiles mixed with water, and Jews drank it. He saw lupine beans that gentiles cooked, and Jews ate them. He did not say anything to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about three things רבי חייא בר אבא saw in a town called גבלא. This sets up the next step, where he reports to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story describes three separate cases: a conversion that was left unfinished, wine that gentiles handled, and food that gentiles cooked. The story stresses that רבי חייא בר אבא stayed silent. That silence is what makes רבי יוחנן's strong reaction in the next step stand out.

keyTerms.meaning: happened to come to a place
were circumcised but did not immerse in a מקוה (an unfinished conversion)
lupine beans, which must be cooked before eating

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְגַבְלָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba happened to come to Gavla.
He saw Jewish women who were pregnant
from gentiles who had been circumcised but had not immersed.
He saw wine that gentiles diluted
and Jews drank it.
He saw lupine beans that gentiles cooked
and Jews ate them.
And he did not say anything at all to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְגַבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, unrelated to the water and boulders discussion in steps 1-5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The story sets out three cases of lax practice in Gavla.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן orders three strict announcements
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רבי חייא בר אבא to announce that the children are ממזרים, that the wine is forbidden as יין נסך, and that the lupines are forbidden as בישולי גוים, because the people there are not בני תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן told him: Go and announce that their children are ממזרים. Announce that their wine is forbidden because of יין נסך. Announce that their lupines are forbidden because of בישולי גוים. Do this because they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא reports what he saw. רבי יוחנן gives a strict ruling on each of the three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each problem gets its own ruling: the children are ממזרים, the wine is forbidden, and the lupines are forbidden. The closing reason, that they are not בני תורה, belongs to the lupines. The next steps show that the ממזר ruling follows רבי יוחנן's own view of the law and the wine ban is a fence ('stay far from the vineyard').

keyTerms.meaning: children born from a forbidden union, who may not marry into the regular community
wine used for idol worship, and the related ban on gentiles' wine
the rabbinic ban on food cooked by gentiles
people who are learned in Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: The reason 'they are not בני תורה' shows that a community's level of knowledge can affect how strict a ruling must be.

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yochanan.
He said to him: Go and announce
about their children that they are mamzerim,
and about their wine, that it is forbidden because of libation wine,
and about their lupines, that they are forbidden because of food cooked by gentiles,
because they are not people of Torah.
phrases.notes: He means they don't know the הלכה well, so a lenient ruling might get stretched too far.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צֵא וְהַכְרֵז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's ruling on the three cases described in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The children are ממזרים, the wine is forbidden as יין נסך, and the lupines are forbidden as בישולי גוים, the last because the community is not בני תורה.

steps.title: Why the children are ממזרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן is following his own two rulings. A convert is not a convert until he immerses, so these men are still gentiles. And a gentile who fathers a child with a Jewish woman produces a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: About calling the children ממזרים: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. רבי יוחנן said that a person is never a convert until he is circumcised and immerses. Since these men did not immerse, they are gentiles. And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן that if a gentile or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first announcement. It shows that calling the children ממזרים comes straight from two other rulings of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation works like a chain with two links. First, conversion needs both circumcision and immersion, so these men are still gentiles. Second, רבי יוחנן holds that a child of a gentile and a Jewish woman is a ממזר. Put together, the children of Gavla are ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning from elsewhere
he will immerse in a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: Calling the child of a gentile a ממזר is רבי יוחנן's own position, as the גמרא says ('לטעמיה'). Do not assume everyone agrees with it.

phrases.english: About their children, that they are mamzerim —
Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person is never a convert
until he is circumcised and immerses,
and since he did not immerse, he is a gentile.
And Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: A gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman —
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל בְּנֵיהֶם שֶׁהֵם מַמְזֵרִים — רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the three announcements in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Conversion needs both circumcision and immersion. A child born to a gentile and a Jewish woman is a ממזר, according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Why the diluted wine is forbidden: stay far from the vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the wine decree with the saying 'go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard.' A strict fence is placed far from the actual prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And decree on their wine because of יין נסך': this is because of the saying, 'Go, go, we tell the נזיר; go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second announcement. The wine is forbidden as a protective fence, even though only diluting it was involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Diluting wine is not the same as the gentile actually touching it for worship, so one might think it is fine. The גמרא answers with a saying: a נזיר, who may not drink wine, is told to keep away from the vineyard altogether. In the same way, Jews are kept far from anything close to יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: a נזיר, who is forbidden to drink wine
go around, go around (keep your distance)

steps.whatToRemember: The three גבלא rulings have different bases. The ממזר ruling is רבי יוחנן's own view of the law. The wine decree rests on 'stay far from the vineyard.' The lupine ban (steps 10-12) is because they are not בני תורה.

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזוּר עַל יֵינָם מִשּׁוּם יֵין נֶסֶךְ —
phrases.english: And decree on their wine because of libation wine —
because of the saying: "Go, go, we say to the nazir;
phrases.notes: This is a popular saying. A נזיר can't drink wine, so he's told not to even walk near grapes.

phrases.english: go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזוּר עַל יֵינָם מִשּׁוּם יֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second announcement from step 7, just as step 8 explained the first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine that gentiles only diluted might seem permitted, since it was not used for worship.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden as a fence, keeping people far from anything close to יין נסך, like the נזיר who stays away from the vineyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine that gentiles diluted is forbidden as a fence around יין נסך, based on the saying 'go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard.'

steps.title: Quoting the lupine part of רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the third part of רבי יוחנן's instruction: the lupines are forbidden as בישולי גוים because the people are not בני תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about their lupines, they are forbidden because of food cooked by gentiles, since they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the third item in רבי יוחנן's ruling, the lupines, so it can examine it. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine was already explained in the last step. Now the גמרא repeats the lupine line because it wants to look closely at its reason: 'since they are not בני תורה.'

keyTerms.meaning: Lupines, bitter beans that must be cooked before eating
Food cooked by a non-Jew, which the רבנן forbade
People who know Torah and keep its laws carefully

phrases.english: And regarding their lupines
they are forbidden because of food cooked by gentiles
since they are not people of Torah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the wine decree, the גמרא turns to the lupine decree from the same ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lupines of גבלא are forbidden as בישולי גוים because the people there are not בני תורה.

steps.title: Lupines should be forbidden for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the reason to mean lupines are allowed for בני תורה. But רב said only food eaten raw is free from בישולי גוים, and lupines are not eaten raw, so they should be forbidden for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that they are not people of Torah. That means for people of Torah it would be allowed? But רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב: anything eaten raw, the way it is, is not included in בישולי גוים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי יוחנן's words and then challenges it with a rule of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'because they are not בני תורה' suggests that lupines are really permitted, and only these people are being made stricter. But by רב's rule, only food eaten raw is exempt. Lupines cannot be eaten raw, so they should be fully forbidden even for בני תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But then', introducing an inference from what was just said

phrases.english: The reason is that they are not people of Torah
but for people of Torah it would be permitted?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak say that Rav said
Anything that is eaten as it is, raw
is not subject to the ban on food cooked by gentiles!
phrases.notes: Lupines are too bitter to eat raw, so this rule would forbid them for everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאֵינָן בְּנֵי תוֹרָה, הָא בְּנֵי תוֹרָה שְׁרֵי? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the lupine line and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of רבי יוחנן's words that lupines are permitted for בני תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב, only food eaten raw is exempt. Lupines are not eaten raw, so they should be forbidden for everyone, not only for people who are not בני תורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows the 'table of kings' version
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds the other version of רב's rule: food not served on a king's table with bread is not included in בישולי גוים. Lupines are such a food, so they are really permitted, and only the unlearned people of גבלא were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds like the other version, where רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב: anything not served on the table of kings as a side dish with bread is not included in בישולי גוים. So the reason is that they are not people of Torah, but for people of Torah it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רב's rule exists in two versions, and רבי יוחנן follows the one that leaves lupines permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, the test is not 'raw or cooked' but 'is this food important?' Lupines are a simple food that kings would not serve, so they are not included in בישולי גוים. That is why the inference stands: lupines are allowed in general, and the people of גבלא got a stricter rule only because they were not בני תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, this is his opinion
The table of kings, a test for whether a food is important
To eat as a side dish together with bread

steps.confusionAlert: Torah scholars do not have a separate law here. Lupines really are permitted. The ban in גבלא was an extra fence, because people who are not בני תורה might come to be lenient with truly forbidden foods.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב's rule on בישולי גוים: (1) food eaten raw is exempt; (2) food not served on a king's table with bread is exempt. רבי יוחנן follows the second.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two tests, 'eaten raw' and 'table of kings,' are the basic rules for what is included in בישולי גוים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הָךְ לִישָּׁנָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan holds like that other version

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב
phrases.english: as Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said that Rav said

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה לְשׁוּלְחָן שֶׁל מְלָכִים
phrases.english: Anything that is not served on the table of kings
to be eaten together with bread
is not subject to the ban on food cooked by gentiles
So the reason is that they are not people of Torah
but for people of Torah it is permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הָךְ לִישָּׁנָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by pointing to another version of רב's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate version of the source: רבי יוחנן follows the second version of רב's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule exempts only food eaten raw, so lupines would be forbidden for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under the 'table of kings' version, lupines are exempt. They are permitted for בני תורה and forbidden in גבלא only as a fence.

steps.title: May a גוי carry grapes to the winepress?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is put to רב כהנא: may a גוי bring grapes to the winepress?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב כהנא: a גוי, what is the law about letting him carry grapes to the winepress?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. Sages ask רב כהנא whether a גוי may help by carrying grapes to the winepress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גוי is not touching wine. He is only carrying grapes before any wine is made. The question is whether even this early step must be kept away from a גוי.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Kahana
A gentile: what is the law about his carrying grapes to the winepress?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new discussion about a גוי's involvement in making wine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a גוי may bring grapes to the winepress.

steps.title: רב כהנא forbids it as a fence
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says it is forbidden, based on the saying 'go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It is forbidden, because of the saying 'Go, go, we tell the נזיר; go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that the גוי may not carry the grapes, and he gives the same 'keep far away' saying used earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying grapes is not making יין נסך. But it brings the גוי close to the wine, so the רבנן keep him away, the way a נזיר is told to stay away from the vineyard completely.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר, who may not have any grape products
Go around, go around (keep your distance)

phrases.english: He said to them: It is forbidden
because of 'Go, go, we tell the nazir
go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about a גוי carrying grapes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden as a protective fence, keeping far from יין נסך.

steps.title: רב יימר begins a challenge from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר challenges רב כהנא with a ברייתא about a גוי who brought grapes to the winepress in baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר raised an objection to רב כהנא: a גוי who brought grapes to the winepress in baskets...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר starts to challenge רב כהנא by quoting a ברייתא. The quote continues past this point, so this line sets up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about the same case, a גוי bringing grapes to the winepress. Its ruling, which comes on the next amud, is what will be used against רב כהנא's ban.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar raised an objection to Rav Kahana
A gentile who brought grapes to the winepress in baskets

steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that a גוי may not bring grapes to the winepress.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא discusses a גוי who brought grapes to the winepress in baskets. Its ruling, which comes next, will be used against רב כהנא's ban.
